en.name: Alexander VI
en.summary: The Borgia pope whose flagrant nepotism, political scheming, and family scandals made him the byword for Renaissance papal corruption.
en.body: Rodrigo Borgia used a fortune amassed as a cardinal to secure his election, then advanced his children Cesare and Lucrezia Borgia to extraordinary power, using marriage alliances and military conquest to carve out territory for the Borgia family in central Italy. His pontificate is remembered for lavish court life, ruthless politics, and the 1493 bull dividing newly discovered lands between Spain and Portugal. Even by the standards of his era his reputation for venality and violence was extreme, and it did lasting damage to the papacy's moral authority on the eve of the Reformation.
